row.evidence: Island publishes no prices ('how we price Island based on your unique needs'), and its Okta OIN app and Microsoft's Entra tutorial both document SCIM user provisioning into Island.
row.notes: Quote-only: Island (the Enterprise Browser) has no public plans; every deal goes through a custom quote. Island's own documentation is login-only (documentation.island.io redirects to login.island.io; the support page says the knowledge base is in the admin portal), so SCIM facts come from IdP pages: Okta's OIN app (last updated Aug. 20 2025) does SAML + SCIM create, update, deactivate and group push, and Microsoft's Entra gallery app provisions users and groups via a tenant URL and secret token once Island support enables it. The SCIM plan gate therefore rests on IdP pages plus the quote-only pricing, hence confidence low. scim_ops left null because no vendor doc describes the operations. Microsoft's SSO tutorial also says Island supports JIT on SSO.

limitations.text: Entra provisioning must first be configured by Island support.

scim.notes: SCIM evidence comes only from the IdP catalogue pages (Okta OIN SCIM app; Microsoft's Entra provisioning tutorial with a tenant URL and secret token). Island's own admin documentation sits behind the customer login, so endpoints, operations and attributes are not recorded here from first-party sources.

user_api.notes: Island's documentation and any management API reference are behind the customer login (documentation.island.io redirects to login.island.io).

okta.notes: OIN capabilities read from page markup: SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push, Universal Logout (last updated Aug. 20 2025).

entra.notes: Gallery app: SSO (SP and IdP initiated, JIT) and automatic user and group provisioning; mapped user attributes userName, active, displayName, title, emails[type eq "work"].value, preferredLanguage, name.givenName, name.familyName, name.formatted, externalId; group attributes displayName, externalId, members. Island support must enable provisioning first.

fallbacks.notes: Microsoft's SSO tutorial says Island supports JIT user provisioning (c9), but no Island page confirms it.
